entities.summary: Bobby Frank Rule was an American professional basketball player. He played at center in the National Basketball Association (NBA) for the Seattle SuperSonics, Philadelphia 76ers, Cleveland Cavaliers, and the Milwaukee Bucks. He was selected to the first team NBA All-Rookie team (1967–68). In his second and third NBA seasons, he was in the top 10 in scoring average. Almost every other player in the top 10 for those two seasons was eventually inducted into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame. His career was derailed in the fourth game of his fourth season by an Achilles tendon injury from which he never fully recovered.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bob Rule's NBA career was notable for his early success, earning him a spot on the first team NBA All-Rookie team in 1967–68. His injury-plagued fourth season had significant regional impact on the Milwaukee Bucks' roster and playoff prospects.
